exposure: heart disease (congenital heart disease, rheumatic heart disease)
cohort: The study included 31 pregnant women with either known or newly diagnosed heart disease.
finding: Among pregnant women with cardiac disease, rheumatic heart disease was most prevalent (27 patients), and foetal outcomes were predominantly live births with 27.4% of babies requiring admission to the neonatal intensive care unit.
mod_finding: The majority of patients underwent vaginal delivery, while 41% underwent caesarean section.
